extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP litigators, Federal Circuit practitioners, and policy/empirical analysts
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical, year‑in‑review analysis of all Federal Circuit patent decisions in 2023, specifying inclusion/exclusion rules and reporting multiple outcome, timing, and judge‑level metrics to characterize the court's patent docket and tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study inclusion and exclusion rules (Methodology and Scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study 'covers all patent cases decided by the Federal Circuit in 2023, whether by precedential opinion, nonprecedential opinion or summary affirmance. It includes merits decisions and rulings on writ petitions, but it excludes denials of leave to appeal, dismissals for lack of finality, stipulated dismissals and remands, and dismissals for mootness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes appeals and writ petitions from district courts, the PTAB, the ITC, and the Court of Federal Claims, but only cases in which the Federal Circuit decided at least one patent law issue. If companion cases are resolved separately they are counted separately; if multiple appeals are decided in a single opinion they are counted as one decision. When an opinion is reissued after rehearing the reissued opinion is counted and the retracted opinion disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-origin categorization (Caseload by venue/type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions are categorized by origin (PTAB, district courts, ITC, Court of Federal Claims) and by PTAB subtypes (inter partes review, post‑grant review, original‑prosecution, ex parte reexamination, inter partes reexamination, interference, reissue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute counts and percentage shares (e.g., PTAB accounted for 59% of decisions; nearly half (47%) were IPRs). Use these categories to detect shifts in docket composition over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmance rate (full affirmance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of cases in which the Federal Circuit 'fully upheld the lower court or agency — i.e., affirmed or dismissed on all issues or denied all relief in mandamus cases.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute overall affirmance rate and break down by origin (PTAB, district court, ITC, etc.). Use as a primary measure of how often the lower tribunal/agency wins on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant success rates and outcome breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Report percentages of cases in which appellants (patent owners/applicants or patent challengers) prevailed outright, lost outright, or produced mixed results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide role‑specific breakdowns (e.g., owners/applicants vs challengers) and venue‑specific comparisons (e.g., owners fare better in district court appeals than in PTAB appeals). Note that when both sides appeal, side‑specific counts may exceed total case counts (the study treats each side's appeal separately when reporting these statistics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of opinions and disposition categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify decisions as precedential opinions, nonprecedential opinions, or summary dispositions and report their relative frequencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define summary dispositions (most are single‑line decision orders under Federal Circuit Rule 36; the author also treats other decisions of a page or less as summary dispositions, including cases where the court affirms on one ground without reaching others). Report trends in the rates of each opinion type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity — docket‑to‑decision timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Median time from docketing to date of decision for true appeals (excluding writ petitions) is used as a productivity metric (e.g., median increased from 12.7 months in 2021 to 16.8 months in 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also report median lag time from the ready date (typically submission of a compliant joint appendix) to oral argument or submission on the papers. Track trends over time and note operational factors (e.g., number of courtrooms) that may affect timings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑argument decision timing by opinion type
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure median time from oral argument or submission on the papers to issuance of opinion, broken down by opinion type (e.g., precedential panel opinions median 3 months; nonprecedential opinions other than summary affirmances median 1.1 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to assess how quickly the court produces written dispositions after submission; report by opinion type and compare across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge‑level activity and speed metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report per‑judge statistics such as number of patent cases decided, opinions authored (precedential vs nonprecedential), and median time to produce opinions (e.g., Judges Taranto and Lourie quickest for precedential decisions; Judge Dyk fastest for nonprecedential decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include counts of decisions authored and total patent decisions per judge; use medians to compare speed across judges and identify outliers in productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: En banc activity and panel dissent rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Track whether the court heard patent cases en banc and measure the rate of panel dissents (e.g., no patent en banc decisions 2019–2023; dissents dropped from 8.3% in 2022 to 4.6% in 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report scheduled rehearings en banc separately and explain factors affecting dissent rates (for 2023 the suspension of frequent dissenter Judge Pauline Newman was noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 101 (patent‑eligibility) case counts and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Count the number of patent‑eligibility cases decided and report outcomes (affirmed, reversed, mixed) and appellant identity (e.g., all 19 Section 101 appeals were by patentees; the court fully affirmed in 16 of them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to assess trends in patent‑eligibility jurisprudence and patentees' success rates on §101 issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent‑Friendliness Index (PFI) — construction and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: PFI defined as '100 plus the percentage of decisions entirely favoring the patent owner or patent applicant less the percentage of decisions entirely against the patent owner or patent applicant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude mixed decisions and dissents from denials of rehearing en banc from the calculation. Note caveats: PFI is a rough measure because of random distribution of cases among judges, exclusion of mixed outcomes, and equal weighting of all cases regardless of significance or issues raised. Use PFI to compare overall court tendencies and judge‑level tilt toward patentees or challengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting rules for companion cases, multiple appeals, and reissued opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the court resolves companion cases separately, count decisions separately; if the court decides multiple appeals in a single opinion, count as one decision. When the Federal Circuit reissues an opinion after granting rehearing, count the reissued opinion and disregard the retracted opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these counting rules consistently to avoid double‑counting and to reflect the court's final, operative dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to treat summary dispositions and very short orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat most Rule 36 single‑line decision orders as summary dispositions; also treat other decisions of a page or less as summary dispositions (for example, decisions that simply announce affirmation on one ground without reaching others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such orders in the summary disposition category when reporting opinion‑type frequencies, and note that counting them may affect the apparent rate of nonprecedential/summary outcomes.
